stem.text: The volume of water in a tank is V(t) liters, t minutes after a valve is opened. Suppose that \( V''(6) = 8 \). Write this statement in Leibniz notation, and state what it means.

answer_key.label: \( \left. \frac{d^{2}V}{dt^{2}} \right|_{t=6} = 8 \), so the rate of change, with respect to time, of the rate of change of the volume of water when t = 6 is 8 liters per minute per minute.

worked_solution.text: In \( V''(6) \) the function is V, the independent variable is t, and the second derivative is evaluated at t = 6, so the statement is about one input only.
In Leibniz notation the same statement is \( \left. \frac{d^{2}V}{dt^{2}} \right|_{t=6} = 8 \).
It says that the rate of change, with respect to time, of the rate of change of the volume of water when t = 6 is 8 liters per minute per minute.

options.label: \( \left. \frac{d^{2}V}{dt^{2}} \right|_{t=6} = 8 \), so the rate of change, with respect to time, of the rate of change of the volume of water when t = 6 is 8 liters per minute per minute.
\( \left(\frac{dV}{dt}\right)^{2} = 8 \text{ at } t = 6 \), so the square of the rate of change of the volume of water with respect to time when t = 6 is 8 liters squared per minute squared.
options.derivation: the second derivative written as the square of the first derivative

options.label: \( \frac{d^{2}V}{dt^{2}} = 8 \), so the rate of change, with respect to time, of the rate of change of the volume of water, the same at every t, is 8 liters per minute per minute.
options.derivation: the point of evaluation dropped, so a value at one input is read as the second derivative function

options.label: \( \left. \frac{d^{2}t}{dV^{2}} \right|_{t=6} = 8 \), so the rate of change, with respect to the volume of water, of the rate of change of time when t = 6 is 8 minutes per liter per liter.
options.derivation: the roles of the two variables exchanged, so the derivative is read with respect to the dependent variable
